newsitem.title: UK: UK privatised industry chiefs attacked over rewards.
newsitem.headline: UK privatised industry chiefs attacked over rewards.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party on Tuesday attacked huge rewards for the heads of privatised industries, claiming three directors of a railway company were set to receive a bonanza when it is taken over.
Labour leader Tony Blair told parliament the directors of train leasing company Eversholt Leasing would between them make windfall profits of at least 35 million pounds ($56 million).
British press reports said Eversholt, which leases trains to passenger rail companies, is about to be taken over by Forward Leasing, a unit of HSBC Holdings.
Blair said he understood the deal would be for some 900 million pounds, compared with the 580 million that then state-owned railway operator, British Rail, got for it at the end of 1995.
"Such profits are entirely unjustified," he told Prime Minister John Major during parliamentary question time.
"Most people in this country will see the difference between making an honest profit and profiteering."

Blair said he understood Eversholt managing director Andrew Jukes, who invested 110,000 pounds in the firm, would make between 15 and 20 million pounds on the deal, expected to be announced on Wednesday.
Engineering director Roger Aylward and finance director Colin Habgood would each make 10 million pounds.
Blair's attack was the latest in a series on the salaries and perks of directors of companies privatised in recent years by the Conservative government.
But Prime Minister John Major said Blair's criticism on Tuesday had shown his rhetoric about supporting free enterprise and competition was false. ($1=.6227 Pound)
